title: Twelve Days on Denali
excerpt: A four-person team battles whiteout conditions and extreme cold to complete the West Buttress route on North America's highest peak.
full: The team spent twelve days moving between camps on Denali's West Buttress, pinned down for three of those days by a storm that dropped visibility to a few metres. Careful rationing of food and fuel, combined with a disciplined turnaround policy, allowed them to wait out the weather and summit on a rare clear morning, descending safely before the next system arrived.

title: A Quiet Ascent of Ama Dablam
excerpt: Two climbers forgo a large support team for a lightweight, self-sufficient attempt on one of the Himalaya's most striking peaks.
full: Choosing a minimalist approach, the pair carried their own gear between camps and fixed only short sections of rope on the most exposed pitches. Their lighter loads let them move quickly through the technical Mushroom Ridge section, reaching the summit in clear, calm conditions before a fast, careful descent.

title: First Winter Attempt on a Patagonian Spire
excerpt: A three-person team takes advantage of a rare weather window to attempt a technical granite spire in the depths of the Patagonian winter.
full: Patagonia's notoriously unstable weather forced the team to wait nearly three weeks at base camp for a viable window. When a 36-hour gap in the wind finally appeared, they climbed continuously through the night, using headlamps on the crux pitches to reach the summit ridge as the sun rose, before a rapid rappel descent ahead of the next storm front.
